before:
pstack is built for Cursor, and it also installs in Claude Code with `/plugin marketplace add cursor/plugins`, then `/plugin install pstack@cursor-plugins`. There, each command takes a `pstack:` prefix, such as `/pstack:poteto-mode`. The [Claude Code adapter](../../docs/harness/claude-code.md) maps the Cursor names, and a step that needs a Cursor-only feature, such as Bugbot or Automations, is skipped with a one-line note.

Other tools can read the skills, because they use the Agent Skills format. But most workflow skills, including `/poteto-mode`, `/how`, `/why`, and `/teach`, spawn Cursor subagents with per-role models, and Custom Modes and `/loop` are Cursor features, so those parts may not work there.
after: This profile runs on OpenCode V2 and provides native skill commands, per-role subagent models, persistent modes, timers, event wakes and webhook routines. It does not require a platform-instruction adapter. Read [PORTING.md](../../PORTING.md) for verified coverage and unfinished work. Hosted cloud VMs and a hosted project dashboard are not supplied: a step that requires that isolation or remote service must stay explicitly blocked until the real prerequisite is available, not be silently replaced by a local approximation.

before:
Whether `/poteto-mode` stays on depends on how the user starts it:

- Enter on `/poteto-mode` attaches the skill to one message. It fades as the chat moves on.
- Option+Enter on Mac or Alt+Enter on Windows, or Use as Mode from the skill entry, makes it a Custom Mode. It stays in context every turn until the user exits the mode, and it stays out of casual turns.
- Cursor's docs list Custom Modes in the Agents Window and the CLI. Elsewhere, start each new task with `/poteto-mode`.

Link [Cursor's skills docs](https://cursor.com/docs/skills) when this comes up. Mid-chat, "new task" makes the mode match a fresh playbook. `/poteto-mode` already uses `poteto-agent` for the subagents its playbook steps spawn. To get the same style from a subagent of your own, spawn it with `subagent_type: "poteto-agent"`.
after:
Whether `/poteto-mode` stays on depends on how the user starts it:

- `/poteto-mode <task>` loads the skill for that request.
- `/pstack-mode on poteto-mode` keeps the full native skill in session instructions across turns, compaction and service restarts. Then send the task normally. Add a personal mode ID after it to keep both active.
- `/pstack-mode off` removes persistent instructions. `/pstack-mode status` reports the selection. These settings are explicit user commands and do not make every skill autoinvoke.

Mid-chat, "new task" makes the mode match a fresh playbook. `/poteto-mode` uses `poteto-agent` for the delegates inside its playbook steps. To request that style for another delegate, use native `subagent` with `agent: "poteto-agent"`, the appropriate required `role`, and `background: true`.

Companion and runtime features:

- `/deslop`, `control-cli`, and `control-ui` are bundled companion skills.
- `/create-skill` is the native authoring helper. `/loop` is the native scheduling command backed by `pstack_schedule`; a running OpenCode service delivers its wakes.
- pstack has no `/orchestrate` skill. Orchestrate is a `/poteto-mode` playbook. If the slash menu shows `/orchestrate`, another plugin provides it.
